issues.kind: source-side line anchors follow the ARVO build image, not the declared vulnerable_commit (uniform +10 offset)
issues.description: Every ParsePowerRails-internal anchor (entry 851, Decoder evt 852, for-loop 854, RailDescriptor 855, idx 857, size guard 858, resize 859, sink 863) matches the compiled ARVO image and sanitizer_trace.txt exactly (sink 863:33, dispatch 306). But the DECLARED vulnerable source in patch.diff (hunk `@@ -841,31 +841,36 @@`, i.e. vulnerable_commit a59cff1e = parent of fix) places the identical code strings 10 lines earlier: ParsePowerRails opens at 841, `Decoder evt` 842, `auto idx = desc.index()` 847, `if (power_rails_strs_id_.size() <= idx)` 848, `resize(idx + 1)` 849, and the `power_rails_strs_id_[idx] = ...` sink at 853. All file/function/code strings match verbatim and the internal line spacing is identical; only the absolute numbers are offset +10. This is not a semantic defect (the GT is self-consistent and agrees with the artifact that actually crashes), but a human verifying source-side anchors against vulnerable_commit a59cff1e will see a systematic mismatch, and the GT never states which tree its numbers follow.

issues.kind: GT embeds a raw PoC byte fragment
issues.description: The GT quotes the literal index varint `08 ff ff ff ff ff 20` (the RailDescriptor.index field encoding) in tainted_value_origin.note and poc.trigger. Per the agent contract, ground_truth.json must not include original PoC bytes. The fragment is only one field's encoding (not a usable standalone PoC), but it is nonetheless a verbatim slice of the reproducer and would read more cleanly as a semantic statement (idx = UINT32_MAX / 0xFFFFFFFF). Low severity because it leaks no exploit recipe and the decoded value is the load-bearing fact.

review_notes: Source (criteria 1-2): source is the project parse point `protos::pbzero::PowerRails::Decoder evt(blob.data, blob.size)` in ProtoTraceParser::ParsePowerRails, NOT the fuzz harness. LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput / FuzzTraceProcessor are explicitly and correctly rejected in source.note. Code string matches the vulnerable function body verbatim (present in patch.diff context).

tainted_value_origin (criterion 3): idx = desc.index() is the first concrete vulnerability-relevant tainted value (the uint32 that becomes the OOB subscript). VERIFIED against the PoC bytes: the RailDescriptor.index varint `ff ff ff ff ff 20` has all of bits 0-34 set, so its low 32 bits are 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. idx = UINT32_MAX. The GT's idx = 0xFFFFFFFF claim is correct.

Integer-overflow characterization is CORRECT and patch-supported: the patch changes `auto idx` to `uint32_t idx`, confirming idx is a 32-bit unsigned. `idx + 1` for idx == 0xFFFFFFFF is computed in uint32 arithmetic and wraps to 0 BEFORE the size_t conversion in resize(idx + 1), so resize(0) leaves the vector empty and the subsequent store power_rails_strs_id_[idx] is out of bounds. This is a textbook integer-overflow-to-buffer-overflow (CWE-190/191 -> CWE-787), faithfully described in classification / bug_description / root_cause / fine_trace step 7.

parser_admitted (criterion 4): ParseTracePacket has_power_rails() dispatch (line 306) is a distinct, earlier container-acceptance checkpoint separate from the final source, and matches ASan crash-stack frame #1.

fine_trace (criteria 5-6): genuine 8-step data/control-flow trace (dispatch -> Decoder source -> rail_descriptor iterate -> RailDescriptor decode -> idx materialization -> missing-bound guard/root_cause -> overflowing resize -> OOB store), not a call stack. depends_on edges (data via blob/evt/it/desc/idx; control via idx>256 and size<=idx) are real and correctly ordered. Both the size expression (resize idx+1, step 7) and the downstream memory op (store, step 8) are represented, satisfying the integer/size bug-class coverage requirement.

root_cause (criterion 7): well supported by patch.diff -- the fix inserts `if (PERFETTO_UNLIKELY(idx > 256)) { PERFETTO_DLOG(...); continue; }` immediately before the size guard, i.e. it adds exactly the missing upper bound on the attacker-controlled idx that root_cause names. Description explains the concrete mechanism (unbounded idx used to both size and subscript the vector, with idx+1 wrapping to 0), not 'the crash disappears'.

sanitizer_ground_truth faithfully reproduces sanitizer_trace.txt: SEGV wild-addr-read, crash_address 0x0000ffff7fff, SCARINESS 20, fault at proto_trace_parser.cc:863:33, and the OSS-Fuzz-classified-UNKNOWN-WRITE vs ASan-reported-READ discrepancy is explicitly and correctly reconciled in access_type (LHS vector-element store; ASan decodes the raw DEADLYSIGNAL as a read). crash_stack frames match the trace (863/306/136/229/34/43).

poc.format is a format/reachability contract only (perfetto Trace protobuf; TracePacket sets power_rails; PowerRails has >=1 rail_descriptor with index > 256 large enough that resize(idx+1) fails to grow the vector) and carries no full PoC or exploit recipe; see the low-severity note on the embedded index-varint fragment elsewhere in the GT.

No bootstrap wording (first-pass / selected as / requires review) in any final GT field; the single 'candidate PoC' mention is inside poc.format.contract, which is the intended PoC-evaluation contract.
Not re-checked here (belongs to stage 05 runtime validation): actual reachability, runtime taint flow, and the concrete crash -- already witnessed by sanitizer_trace.txt / reachability_report.json.

Note on provenance: the previous static_review.json on disk (pre-dating the current ground_truth.json) asserted idx = 0x0FFFFFFF with no integer overflow. That was incorrect -- direct decoding of the PoC index varint yields 0xFFFFFFFF -- and has been superseded by this review.
